title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.25964v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark. The LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline we measured, 82.21 F1 on the adversarial split, sat 1.21 to 8.67 points above the adversarial baselines we planned to compare against (81.00, 79.30, and 73.54). We looked at the evaluation code and found a readout choice that moves F1 on its own. A two-token logit readout decides yes versus no by comparing two vocabulary IDs, 3582 ("yes") and 1217 ("no"). Across 9,000 greedy-decode questions spanning all three splits, neither ID is generated even once. The model emits " Yes" (token 3869) and " No" (token 1939), because SentencePiece prepends a space byte after the prompt suffix "ASSISTANT:". Read with an eight-token lookup that covers the space-prefixed surface forms, LLaVA-1.5-7B scores F1 0.8221, 0.8498, and 0.8713 on the adversarial, popular, and random splits. translated_title: 词元集合选择混淆POPE基准：VLM幻觉评估中是/否提取的系统性审计
translated_abstract: 我们试图复现POPE基准上近期的一个幻觉缓解结果。我们测得的LLaVA-1.5-7B基线在对抗性分割上达到82.21 F1，比我们计划对比的对抗性基线（81.00、79.30和73.54）高出1.21至8.67分。我们检查了评估代码，发现一个仅凭自身就能改变F1分数的读出选择：双词元logit读出方式通过比较两个词表ID——3582（"yes"）和1217（"no"）——来判定是与否。但在跨越全部三个分割的9,000个贪心解码问题上，这两个ID一次也从未被生成过。模型实际输出的是“ Yes”（词元3869）和“ No”（词元1939），因为SentencePiece在提示词后缀"ASSISTANT:"之后会前置一个空格字节。改用覆盖带空格前缀表层形式的八字元查找来读取结果时，LLaVA-1.5-7B在对抗性、热门和随机分割上的F1分别为0.8221、0.8498和0.8713。仅这一对抗性分割上的6.13分偏移就超过了……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文系统审计了POPE幻觉评估中的是/否答案提取方式，发现传统双词元logit读出所比较的"yes"/"no"词元ID在LLaVA-1.5-7B的实际输出中从未出现过（模型实际生成的是带空格前缀的" Yes"/" No"），仅这一读出实现细节就能使F1分数偏移高达6.13分，说明评估代码的实现选择会严重混淆基准对比结论。
en_tdlr: A systematic audit of yes/no extraction in POPE hallucination evaluation reveals that the standard two-token logit readout compares token IDs ("yes"/"no") that LLaVA-1.5-7B never actually generates—it emits space-prefixed " Yes"/" No" tokens—and this single readout choice alone shifts F1 by up to 6.13 points, confounding hallucination-mitigation benchmark comparisons.
